missing_criteria: SC-15 defines the judgment unit by naming separators. The round shows that is the wrong shape of definition: the unit question recurs at `|&` (a separator spelling), inside `{ }`/`if..fi` groups and `while` loops (a sub-unit below the pipeline), and at process substitution (a data flow with no separator at all). The criterion should define the unit by DATA FLOW — 'if the shell makes one command's output the input of another, or carries one command's argument into another (`$_`), they are one judgment unit' — and require the separator/construct pool to be DERIVED from the splitter's own branch table, exactly as SC-12(3) already requires for notation pools.
No criterion covers the shell's implicit operand carriers (`$_`, and in interactive shells `!$`/`!!`). SC-15(2)'s justification asserts they do not exist.
ambiguous_criteria: SC-14(2) lists permission removal in the same effect grade as deletion, while SC-14(3) exempts any effect whose plain spelling is allow. `chmod 000 hooks/hooks.json` is allow and is filed under `no_floor_effects` on the strength of (3). The two clauses point opposite ways for the same cell; the resolution should be to raise the plain spelling, not to keep exempting it. Not counted against this round — it is a registered, pre-existing residual — but it will keep absorbing findings until it is settled.
security_criteria_insufficient: SC-15(2)'s claim that newline splits is contradicted by both splitter paths; the criterion and the code should be reconciled in whichever direction is intended.

residual_judgment.reasoning: Two of the open families are named inside the criterion this round was written to satisfy (`|&` in SC-15(2), `while read` in SC-15(5)), so they are in scope by construction, not deferred scope. All of them keep the control-plane path in the command string, which is the boundary the 43rd verdict explicitly ruled is NOT covered by `indirect_operand`. All are lab-confirmed to delete or zero the wiring, and the plain spelling of each is ask, so each is a direct SC-14(1) floor violation. Fairness note that does not change the verdict: every open family is pre-existing — I measured all of them at fdbcbbc and they were identically allow — so this round introduced no regression. What it did was close one separator spelling of the pipeline axis and then state, in code, docs and contract, that the axis was closed.
